response.title: A Closer Look at Willow Creek
response.passage:
After heavy rain, students at a local high school visited Willow Creek to learn how weather changes a stream. Their science teacher asked them to measure the water at three marked places and note what they saw. The class worked in small groups. Some students held the measuring sticks, while others wrote down the results, so they had to cooperate to finish the survey before lunch.

At the first place, the water looked calm. Farther downstream, it moved quickly around a bend. The students wanted to know whether the water also moved faster near the middle of the stream. They placed small paper boats at the bank and in the center, then watched carefully. The boats in the center traveled farther in the same amount of time. The students recorded the direction and distance rather than guessing from how the water looked.

To make their notes reliable, two students read each measurement aloud while a partner checked it against the marks on the stick. If they disagreed, they measured again and wrote down the new result. Their teacher reminded them that one careful check was more useful than several rushed guesses. The class also kept a copy of the notes at school, so they would still have the results if a page got wet during the trip.

Back in class, the groups compared their records. They found that the center water carried the boats downstream faster than the water near the bank. The teacher asked them to repeat the survey on a dry day. The students planned to compare the results and see whether the stream changed after the rain.

items.answer: Students shared different tasks so they could complete a stream survey together.
distractors: Students worked alone so they could finish their own stream surveys.
Students stopped the survey because the creek was too dangerous to study.
Students spent the visit cleaning the creek instead of measuring its water.
items.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

items.answer: They placed paper boats at the bank and in the center and watched how far they traveled.
distractors: They placed paper boats at the bend and watched how long they stayed there.
They dropped measuring sticks in the stream and watched which ones sank.
They stood on the bank and guessed how quickly the water was moving.
items.question: How did the students observe differences in the water's movement?

items.answer: They checked each measurement against the stick marks and measured again if they disagreed.
distractors: They copied each measurement from memory after leaving the creek.
They accepted the first result even when students disagreed about it.
They asked their teacher to choose results without checking the marks.
items.question: Which detail best explains why the students' notes were reliable?

items.answer: The water in the center carried the boats downstream faster than the water near the bank.
distractors: The water near the bank carried the boats downstream faster than the center water.
The center water carried the boats upstream while the bank water stood still.
The water moved at the same speed near the bank and in the center.
